name: Aleksandr Karelin
one_line: 887 wins, 2 losses, six straight years without conceding a single point - until a dairy farmer beat him 1-0.

facts.claim: career senior record: 887 wins, 2 losses - both losses by a single point, thirteen years apart
facts.note: Loss 1: 1987 USSR Championships (Rostorotsky). Loss 2: Sydney 2000 final. Chart: gold 887 vs gray 2.

facts.claim: unbeaten internationally for 13 years, and no one scored a single point on him in the six years before Sydney 2000
facts.note: Wikipedia verbatim: 'a point had not been scored against him in competition the previous six years.'

facts.claim: three Olympic golds (1988, 1992, 1996) under three different flags - Soviet Union, Unified Team, Russia - and carried the flag at all three ceremonies
facts.note: The country changed around him; the champion did not.

facts.claim: nine world titles and twelve European titles, never losing at either
his signature move, the Karelin Lift, hoisted 130-kilogram opponents off the mat and threw them - a reverse body lift no one else dared use at super-heavyweight
facts.note: Worth maximum points in Greco-Roman. Opponents reportedly preferred conceding position to being thrown. Nicknames: the Russian Bear, the Experiment.

facts.claim: in the Sydney 2000 final he lost 1-0 to American Rulon Gardner - a former dairy farmer who had never won a major international title - and retired
facts.note: The 'Miracle on the Mat'. First points conceded in six years; first loss in thirteen. Gardner grew up doing farm work in Wyoming. Karelin retired after the match.

facts.claim: born 1967 in Novosibirsk, Siberia; after retiring became a member of Russia's parliament
facts.note: Context block: 130kg super-heavyweight, feared across the sport for a decade and a half.

comparison.second_label: career losses - both by one point
comparison.gap_description: 887 wins against 2 losses, thirteen years apart, each by a single point.

story_beat: In the Sydney 2000 final, the man who hadn't conceded a point in six years met Rulon Gardner, an American raised on a dairy farm who had never won a major title. Gardner scored one point and gave up none. Karelin, beaten for the first time in thirteen years, walked off the mat and retired.
